question: Does the short-horizon momentum edge survive conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe?

round-trip probe: zero=909090.9091, slippage-only=909545.4545 (slippage is a net CREDIT), commission-only=909086.9091 (commission is a net COST)
unverified: Robustness to TRUE directional slippage / market impact is UNVERIFIED: the existing engine adds slippage to the fill price on both buys and sells, so slippage is a credit on the closing side and cancels over round trips; the cost test therefore stresses commissions only.

The lookback 3/5/10 grid is near-degenerate: candidate medians are identical across lookbacks for every asset because sign(mean log return over the window) = sign(closes[i]/closes[i-lookback]-1); the grid does not independently stress lookback, so cost results transfer across lookbacks.

The verifier's initial Gate-1 MISMATCH was a verifier-side defect (compared the last segment's fold count against the artifact's first-segment n_folds); fixed and re-run to MATCH. Recorded as a verifier repair, not a research result.
observed_effect: Predeclared edge counts (REGIME_STABLE & all segment medians>0) by cost level: zero 6/6/5, realistic 6/6/6, conservative 6/7/7 (lookbacks 3/5/10) -> OVERALL COST_ROBUST. Candidate per-fold medians are essentially unchanged by cost: zero->conservative decay 0.000 for AAPL/AMZN/GOOGL/JPM/META, 0.001 for JNJ/MSFT/XOM, NVDA 0.024 on a non-edge. The increase in edge counts at conservative cost is a null-dispersion artifact (JPM REGIME_DEPENDENT->REGIME_STABLE because the cost-loaded coin-flip null's cross-segment dispersion grows), not an improvement in the candidate. Cost-model audit: AMZN realistic full-sample 4451 fills, commissions $21,055.22, net slippage cash +$2,189.11 (credit), equity zero $6,537,258 vs realistic $6,518,392 -> drag 1.8866% of capital over 4465 bars (~0.11%/yr), dominated by commissions.
uncertainty_targeted: Does the short-horizon momentum edge survive conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe?
uncertainty_reduced: Cost robustness is now classified: COST_ROBUST for the commission channel of the repository's existing cost model, independently verified and deterministic. What remains uncertain is robustness to true directional slippage, which the existing engine does not actually charge.
research_result: The short-horizon momentum edge (lookback 3/5/10, 1-day hold, daily rebalance) is COST_ROBUST under the repository's existing cost model: realistic and 3x-conservative costs leave candidate per-fold medians essentially unchanged (decay ~0.000-0.001 for 9/10 assets) and the predeclared edge count stays >=6/10 at every lookback. Qualification: the existing engine's slippage is directionally symmetric (a credit on sells) and cancels over round trips, so the tested cost channel is commissions (~0.11%/yr AMZN drag); robustness to true directional slippage/market impact is UNVERIFIED. Process improvement indicated: add a mandatory cost-model audit to the standard gate stack, because the frictionless prior evidence and this model both omit true slippage.
next: Repair the engine's directional slippage sign (charge slippage on sells instead of crediting) and rerun research/checks/momentum_cost_sensitivity.py to test true execution-cost robustness.
